# win32 writes a program in C whose sngl.build names the system it is for, so
# `sngl build` cross-compiles it with MinGW's compiler for that architecture
# and names the program .exe.

[!exec:x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc] skip 'MinGW (x86_64) required'
[!exec:i686-w64-mingw32-gcc] skip 'MinGW (i686) required'

sngl build app.sngl -o out
stdout 'out/app.exe'
[toolchain] exists out/app.exe

# The arch option picks 32-bit Windows, and with it i686's compiler.

sngl build app386.sngl -o out386
stdout 'out386/app.exe'
[toolchain] exists out386/app.exe

-- app.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

output {
    c {
        win32
    }
}

component counter ui.node {
    var n = 0
    ui.button(text="{n}", @click {
        n += 1
    })
}

ui.window(title="count") {
    counter()
}
-- app386.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

output {
    c {
        win32(arch="386")
    }
}

component counter ui.node {
    var n = 0
    ui.button(text="{n}", @click {
        n += 1
    })
}

ui.window(title="count") {
    counter()
}
-- testrun/build/win32/c/app.sngl/1 --
sha256:5f17a0d25141a6200bff8b0fb0f62a83
{
  "stdout": "app.exe"
}
-- testrun/build/win32/c/app386.sngl/1 --
sha256:4e53f78403ca048150c12031a29464ca
{
  "stdout": "app.exe"
}
